title: Property devissage on an irreducible closed support
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme], i.e. locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and let $T\subseteq X$ be an irreducible closed subset with generic point $\xi$ [def-weil-irreducible-components]. Let $\mathcal P$ be a property of coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules [pqf-def-coherent] whose support $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F)=\{x:\mathcal F_x\neq0\}$ [def-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base](2) [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] is contained in $T$, such that (1) for every short exact sequence $0\to\mathcal F_1\to\mathcal F_2\to\mathcal F_3\to0$ of coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules with support contained in $T$, if two out of the three have $\mathcal P$ then so does the third; (2) for every closed immersion $i:Z\to X$ [def-weil-closed-immersion] with $Z$ an integral scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme] and $i(Z)\subsetneq T$, and every quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_Z$, $\mathcal P$ holds for $i_*\mathcal I$ [def-pc-module-pullback]; (3) there is a coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal G$ such that (a) $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal G)=T$, (b) $\mathcal G_\xi$ is annihilated by the maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_\xi\subset\mathcal O_{X,\xi}$ [def-weil-residue-field], (c) $\dim_{\kappa(\xi)}\mathcal G_\xi=1$, and (d) $\mathcal P$ holds for $\mathcal G$. Then $\mathcal P$ holds for every coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal F$ with $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F)\subseteq T$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 01YH (label lemma-property-irreducible, coherent.tex line 3179), including the comparison with G at the generic stalk and the proper-support quotient argument

proof.text: Property $\mathcal P$ is invariant under isomorphism, and if a coherent module with support in $T$ has a finite filtration whose successive quotients have $\mathcal P$, then it has $\mathcal P$, by induction using the two-out-of-three hypothesis (the zero module is handled by the same hypothesis applied to $0\to0\to0\to0$).

If $\mathcal F$ is coherent with $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F)\subseteq T$ and $\xi\notin\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F)$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-filtration-integral-subschemes] to filter $\mathcal F$ by quotients $(i_j)_*\mathcal I_j$. For each short exact sequence in the filtration, exactness on stalks shows $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F_j/\mathcal F_{j-1})\subseteq\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F)$; the nonzero ideal $\mathcal I_j$ has nonzero generic stalk by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-scheme-ideal-generic-stalk], so its support is all of the integral $Z_j$, and the quotient support is the proper irreducible closed subset $i_j(Z_j)\subsetneq T$. Hypothesis (2) gives $\mathcal P$ for each quotient, and Step 1 gives $\mathcal P(\mathcal F)$.

Let $i:Z=T_{\mathrm{red}}\to X$ be the reduced induced closed subscheme structure on $T$ from [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme](2); it is a closed immersion with $Z$ reduced and $i(Z)=T$, so $Z$ is homeomorphic to the nonempty irreducible $T$ and hence integral by the definition [def-pc-integral-scheme], with generic point $\eta$ satisfying $i(\eta)=\xi$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-generic-point-ideal-inclusion] to this $i$ and the sheaf $\mathcal G$ in (3). It gives $r\ge0$, a coherent ideal $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_Z$, and an injection $\alpha:i_*(\mathcal I^{\oplus r})\to\mathcal G$ which is an isomorphism near $\xi$. Since $\mathcal G_\xi$ has dimension one over $\kappa(\xi)$ and a nonzero ideal on the integral $Z$ has generic stalk $\mathcal O_{Z,\eta}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-scheme-ideal-generic-stalk], the generic stalk comparison forces $r=1$ and $\mathcal I\ne0$. Exactness on stalks gives $\operatorname{Supp}(\operatorname{coker}\alpha)\subseteq T$, while the local isomorphism gives zero stalk at $\xi$; hence its support is a proper closed subset of $T$. Step 2 gives property $\mathcal P$ for the cokernel.

For every nonzero quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal I'\subseteq\mathcal I$, form the composite $i_*\mathcal I'\to i_*\mathcal I\xrightarrow{\alpha}\mathcal G$ and let $\mathcal Q'$ be its cokernel. At $\xi$ the map is an isomorphism because both nonzero ideals have generic stalk $\mathcal O_{Z,\eta}$, so exactness on stalks gives $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal Q')\subseteq T$ and $(\mathcal Q')_\xi=0$; thus its support is a proper closed subset of $T$, and Step 2 gives $\mathcal P(\mathcal Q')$. The short exact sequence then gives $\mathcal P(i_*\mathcal I')$ by (1) and the two-out-of-three property.

For any quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal I''\subseteq\mathcal O_Z$, if it is zero then its pushforward is the zero module and has $\mathcal P$. Otherwise $\mathcal I''\cap\mathcal I$ has generic stalk $\mathcal O_{Z,\eta}$ (both factors do, by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-scheme-ideal-generic-stalk]), hence is nonzero on the integral scheme $Z$, so Step 4 gives property for its pushforward. The quotient of $i_*\mathcal I''$ by this intersection has zero generic stalk, and exactness on stalks gives support missing $\xi$; Step 2 gives property for the quotient and (1) gives property for $i_*\mathcal I''$. Hence $\mathcal P$ holds for $i_*\mathcal I''$ for every quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal I''\subseteq\mathcal O_Z$.

Finally, for an arbitrary coherent $\mathcal F$ supported in $T$, use [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-filtration-integral-subschemes]. As in Step 2, each quotient $(i_j)_*\mathcal I_j$ has support $i_j(Z_j)$, an irreducible closed subset of $T$. If $i_j(Z_j)\subsetneq T$ this quotient has $\mathcal P$ by hypothesis (2). If $i_j(Z_j)=T$, then $Z_j$ is integral, hence reduced, and the uniqueness clause [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme](3) gives an isomorphism $\varphi:Z_j\to Z$ with $i\circ\varphi=i_j$; transporting $\mathcal I_j$ along $\varphi$ gives a quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal I''\subseteq\mathcal O_Z$ with $(i_j)_*\mathcal I_j\cong i_*\mathcal I''$, which has $\mathcal P$ by Step 5. Thus every quotient has $\mathcal P$, and Step 1 gives $\mathcal P(\mathcal F)$.

tool_uses.why: The 01YH proof needs the general finite filtration of a coherent module by integral closed-subscheme ideal quotients.
The 01YH proof needs the generic-stalk injection of an ideal pushforward into the distinguished coherent module.
The 01YH proof needs the fact that a nonzero ideal on an integral scheme has full generic stalk, to compare dimensions and intersections.
The 01YH proof needs the integral closed subscheme with underlying set T (Z_0 with its reduced induced structure) and its uniqueness to identify filtration quotients with full support T.

lean.statement: theorem coherent_property_irreducible (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X] (T : Set X) (hTclosed : IsClosed T) (hTirreducible : IsIrreducible T) (ξ : X) (hξ : IsGenericPoint ξ T) (P : X.Modules → Prop) (hshort : ∀ S : ShortComplex X.Modules, S.ShortExact → RingedSpace.IsCoherent X.toRingedSpace S.X₁ → RingedSpace.IsCoherent X.toRingedSpace S.X₂ → RingedSpace.IsCoherent X.toRingedSpace S.X₃ → {x : X | ¬ Subsingleton (S.X₁.presheaf.stalk x)} ⊆ T → {x : X | ¬ Subsingleton (S.X₂.presheaf.stalk x)} ⊆ T → {x : X | ¬ Subsingleton (S.X₃.presheaf.stalk x)} ⊆ T → ((P S.X₁ ∧ P S.X₂) → P S.X₃) ∧ ((P S.X₁ ∧ P S.X₃) → P S.X₂) ∧ ((P S.X₂ ∧ P S.X₃) → P S.X₁)) (hsmaller : ∀ (Z : Scheme.{u}) (i : Z ⟶ X), IsClosedImmersion i → IsIntegral Z → Set.range i.base ⊂ T → ∀ I : Z.IdealSheafData, P ((pushforward i).obj I.toModules)) (hG : ∃ G : X.Modules, RingedSpace.IsCoherent X.toRingedSpace G ∧ {x : X | ¬ Subsingleton (G.presheaf.stalk x)} = T ∧ (∀ a ∈ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (X.presheaf.stalk ξ), ∀ v : (RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor X.toRingedSpace ξ).obj G, a • v = 0) ∧ (∃ inst : Module (X.residueField ξ) ((RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor X.toRingedSpace ξ).obj G), (∀ (a : X.presheaf.stalk ξ) (v : (RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor X.toRingedSpace ξ).obj G), a • v = (X.residue ξ) a • v) ∧ Module.finrank (X.residueField ξ) ((RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor X.toRingedSpace ξ).obj G) = 1) ∧ P G) : ∀ F : X.Modules, RingedSpace.IsCoherent X.toRingedSpace F → {x : X | ¬ Subsingleton (F.presheaf.stalk x)} ⊆ T → P F
